test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A train that has a length of 150 m overtakes a man moving at a speed of 9 km/hr (in the same direction) in 36 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take this train to completely cross another train that is 185 m long, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 43 km/hr?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of Train 1 with respect to the man = Distance ÷ Time = 150 ÷ 36 = 25/6 m/s.

In km/hr, relative speed = (25/6) × (18/5) = 15 km/hr.

Since they move in the same direction, speed of Train 1 = Relative speed + Man's speed = 15 + 9 = 24 km/hr.

Relative speed of Train 1 and Train 2 (opposite direction) = 24 + 43 = 67 km/hr = 67 × (5/18) m/s.

Time to cross = Total Length ÷ Relative Speed = (150 + 185) ÷ [67 × (5/18)] = 335 ÷ (335/18) = 18 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train 1 = 150 m

Speed of the man = 9 km/hr (moving in the same direction)

Time taken to cross the man = 36 seconds

Length of Train 2 = 185 m

Speed of Train 2 = 43 km/hr (moving in the opposite direction)

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S₁ − S₂

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5/18)

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the first train be v km/hr.

⇒ Relative speed with respect to the man = (v − 9) km/hr = (v − 9) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ Time taken to cross the man = Length of Train 1 ÷ Relative speed

⇒ 36 = 150 ÷ [(v − 9) × 5/18]

⇒ v − 9 = (150 × 18) ÷ (36 × 5)

⇒ v − 9 = 2700 ÷ 180

⇒ v − 9 = 15

⇒ v = 24 km/hr

Now, Train 1 crosses Train 2 moving in the opposite direction.

⇒ Total Distance to be covered = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2 = 150 + 185 = 335 m

⇒ Relative speed = Speed of Train 1 + Speed of Train 2

⇒ Relative speed = 24 + 43 = 67 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 67 × 5/18 = 335/18 m/s

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = 335 ÷ (335/18)

⇒ Time taken = (335 × 18) ÷ 335 = 18 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Total Distance in Crossing

When a train crosses a stationary or moving point object (like a man or pole), the total distance covered is merely the length of the train. However, when it crosses another train or platform, the total distance is the sum of the lengths of both objects (L₁ + L₂).

Unit Conversions

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. Conversely, to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5. This conversion is derived from 1 km = 1000 m and 1 hour = 3600 seconds.
